title: | SABBATH EVENING CLASS: Following God's Vision That's Beyond Obscured Eyes

sense.text:
This is an example of a social construct right here in the Bible. A social construct is a concept, and a concept does not have to be based in truth: it can be made up, a figment of the imagination, like a concept car they never bring out on the road. It exists not in objective reality, meaning what is absolute and factual, what you can see from an outside point of view without being brainwashed and twisted. Jesus Christ is black: that is objective reality, we see it, we read it and we accept it. Saying Jesus is white is a concept, not a fact. A social construct exists as a result of human interaction; it exists because humans agree that it exists. They simply agree on a lie.

The human interaction that built this construct was marginalization, persecution and assassinations. You got the truth and the facts, and they say, we are not paying attention to that, and if you keep holding on to it we will marginalize you, persecute you, and go as far as assassinating your leaders. That is why, when we bring the Bible to the churches and the preachers and they see the words, they still say color don’t matter: they are under the grip of a social lying concept.

This chapter is speaking of ancient history, going back to Nimrod and those errors, but it is brought up to the social construct going on now. “Thus in process of time”: it took time to make this happen, time to get humans to agree with a lie, with a concept rather than reality. “An ungodly custom grown strong was kept as a law”: the ungodly custom is the social construct, and they framed it by law.

“Graven images were worshipped by the commandments of kings.” The graven image is that white image you call Christ, the second son of Pope Alexander the Sixth of Rome. He has nothing to do with Judaical or biblical history. He walked the earth as a man, not as Christ; he walked the earth as a homosexual. The people who knew him then did not take him for Jesus; the construct was not heavy yet. But in process of time, as they pushed that image on the people, it grew into a custom grown strong, held up in churches and so-called worship centers and put in your Bibles, and with that repetition over and over you forget what the words say and begin to say, this is what Jesus looks like.

“Whom men could not honour in presence, because they dwelt far off, they took the counterfeit of his visage from far.” The image came out of Rome, so they took the counterfeit image of that man and put it in your churches, your worship centers, your houses, the stores for you to buy, and your so-called Bibles.

“And made an express image”: an exact image. The Bible says Christ is the express image of God, meaning God and Christ look alike; so they took the express image of that man and painted the pictures to look exactly like him. That is why they all look the same: it is the image of one man. You can’t grab any old white man and say this is Jesus; they will say, that ain’t Jesus, bring me the real Jesus. If you don’t have that image as Jesus, and that image in your church, they say you ain’t dealing with Jesus. That’s heavy.

“To the end that by this their forwardness they might flatter him that was absent, as if he were present.” When we hold that picture up and stomp on it, they get as mad as hell, as if the body shots were landing on them. It is a terrible thing to see that kind of reaction over a picture somebody painted that has nothing to do with the Bible.

“Also the singular diligence of the artificer”: the artificer is the artist that painted it, Michelangelo and Leonardo da Vinci. He “did help to set forward the ignorant to more superstition”: the ignorant are the people who believe the picture is Christ when it has nothing to do with Christ, and the painting set them on to more superstitious foolishness.

He “forced all his skill to make the resemblance of the best fashion.” They wanted to fashion that thing perfectly to give more life to it, so our people would be that much more locked into it: stuck on the dashboards of their cars, up on their mantels and walls, thinking Jesus is in there. That’s idolatry, and the Lord killed our people for that foolishness.

“And so the multitude, allured by the grace of the work”: the ignorant multitude, the people in church, allured by the beauty of the painting, “took him now for a god”. They took this homosexual for Jesus Christ, “which a little before was but honoured” as a man, because a little before he was only that son of the pope.
“And this was an occasion to deceive the world”: it was done for the purpose of deceiving the whole world. Who did it? The so-called white man.

precepts.why:
They framed it by law, and that is in the scriptures too. “Shall the throne of iniquity have fellowship with thee”: shall the throne of sin have fellowship with God? In other words, shall the congregation of God allow sin in the body?

“Which frameth mischief by a law.” They put laws around sin, laws around protecting evil. A man talking about he’s a woman: that is a social construct, making everybody believe in something unconnected to objective reality. A man was born a man, and saying he wants to be a woman does not fit in objective reality; it is a concept. If they can get people to agree with the concept and frame a law around it, it becomes as a law. That is the ungodly custom grown strong and kept as a law.

This is who deceived the world, and why the scripture is applied to them. “And the great dragon was cast out”: the great dragon is the so-called white man, and the seven heads and ten horns are all red people. The so-called white man is the true red man; the native American Indians are not red. “That old serpent, called the Devil”: that old spirit of Satan that was back in the garden of Eden. “And Satan, which deceiveth the whole world.”

How did he deceive the whole world? There is no Bible you can pick up with writing in it that says Jesus Christ looks like that image; none of them. Yet they say that’s Jesus. It took major witchcraft, a major social construct, to make people believe it, when the writing in the Bible says Jesus looks like you. The construct was so strong it caused people to leave reality, ignore objective reality and accept a concept.

“He was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him.” When this man goes down, all his lies go down with him. Praise the Lord, we ain’t got to deal with this thing for eternity: the Most High is going to put a stop to it.

“Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? not one.” Nobody can change what the Most High has deemed crooked; if the Lord deemed it crooked you cannot straighten it out. The Most High made this man to be evil, the demon and the devil the Bible speaks of. God made it that way.

“Seeing his days are determined”: God has the number of his months; there is a time limit on him. That is why the scriptures say he knows he has but a short time. “The number of his months are with thee”: the number of this man’s months and of his rulership is with God.

“Thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass.” God has appointed Esau’s ruling boundaries, just as he set the bounds of Babylon’s rulership, then said the same to Persia, then the Greeks from this period to that, then the Romans which came out of the Greeks. God appoints the boundaries of everything. When the Most High turns his lights out it’s done, and there is nothing a negro can do to save him, though he is trying to make this man bend scripture with a social construct. The Bible is the reality, and this reality is going to come to pass.

sense.text:
The class is called Following God’s Vision That’s Beyond Obscured Eyes: eyes in confusion, with the dust they keep up on us to keep us from seeing reality. We live like a lost, confused people who don’t realize they are the product and creation of God. Because of our disobedience the world is running circles and running game on us; we are looking at reality through Esau’s world with the wrong glasses on, and so we are at the bottom of every statistic, losing on every front, as a people not even making our own toilet paper.

“Turn you to the strong hold”: turn you, Israelites, to the stronghold, and the stronghold is the Bible. This is what is missing from our people: we are holding on to a social construct and not to the real standard, which is the Bible. This is what is going to sustain you.

“Ye prisoners of hope.” We are hoping that we can get somewhere in this wicked system, hoping and hoping, and it is never delivered. They did not bring us over here for us to win in our hope. We were brought over here because we broke God’s laws and had to go through punishment, and the Most High put us through it so we can learn what not to do when we repent and the kingdom is set up. When we get out of here, we’re going to get it right.

We are prisoners: in a mental prison, a spiritual prison. We go to church looking to get out of prison and go deeper in. You got the Bible in there, but you have no idea how to unlock it to free your mind, and the preacher makes sure you have the wrong key because he’s on the take.

Being a prisoner of hope is a terrible thing. We keep hoping for some comfort, waiting and begging and praying for it. As we keep wanting these people to do something righteous for us, begging please, please, please, our enemies defer the hope: they take it out of your reach. “Hope deferred” means you can’t reach what you’re hoping for.

“Hope deferred maketh the heart sick”: the heart is the mind. Being prisoners of hope, we beg and pray in these churches under that white image for some hope we are never going to get, so we fathom lies: we’re washed in the blood of Jesus, we’re saved, we’re holy rollers, sanctified, when you know doggone well the society hates your guts. Edomite guys do mass murder shootings and none of them get killed when the police show up, yet our sister Sandra Bland ends up dead over a taillight, and Michael Brown is dead. Whatever they did, none of them did anything near as murderous as Dylann Roof or Peyton, the Buffalo killer.

We are hoping for justice, for some affirmation that we can become first-class citizens. Ask the people in the churches to be honest whether they feel like first-class citizens, and the answer is absolutely no. On a program, a preacher had a man read a letter of threats said to be from the KKK, saying his tongue should be hung out and talking of killing him, and the men and women in that church looked scared over one letter. If a door had slammed they would have run for cover, feeling the Klan was right outside. That is the fear the Bible says our people will be in. First-class citizens don’t feel that. They are afraid of this man because they have not been taught the truth of this Bible. That is why the blitz on that preacher was not to be belligerent to our people: this truth needs to get to the people, and if the preacher won’t deal right with it, it is our obligation to put his feet to the fire. Ezekiel speaks of that obligation: the people he is over are the twelve tribes of Israel, the descendants of those who came over here on the slave ships.

When we can’t get justice, equal rights or equal opportunity, we are automatically second and last priority, the last hired and the first fired. You work four times harder than a so-called white man for a doctorate degree, enduring racism, evil and bigotry, and the further up you go the whiter the room gets. When hope is constantly deferred it drives you mad: it makes the mind sick and frustrates you. You get angry, you take dope, you think something’s wrong with your color, so you bleach your skin and your hair, asking why can’t I be like Susie, like Billy, like Dylan. America is a murderous country: the children of those who murdered, raped and pillaged the original inhabitants are still here reaping the benefits of what their fathers committed. This ain’t hate talk; it is objective reality that everybody knows.

We can’t get a fair shake: a mother asks why her son had to die just walking through a neighborhood eating Skittles, then learns the gun that killed him sold at auction for hundreds of thousands of dollars because the Edomite devil wanted that one gun. (Not ‘the cracker’: that ain’t biblical. The Edomite devil, that’s biblical.)

People in the church say they have faith, but they only have faith in what the so-called white man tells them they can and can’t have, and they say it’s all right in Jesus. Hope deferred makes the mind crazy and aggravates you: maybe I need blonde hair, maybe I need to bleach my skin, talk and look and act like white folks, so they won’t see my color. That is not a social construct; that is objective reality. With the heart made sick come drugs, alcohol, promiscuity, psychiatric admittance and eventually suicide. Our people live suicidally because they don’t see how to get out of this trap, and the preacher is not giving them the answers, so they make up their own: it must be because I’m black, I need to zap the nap. That’s what’s wrong with us.

What should we do? In reality we’re all trying to put hope in this system, and we’re not going to get it. The Lord said this place is not our rest. And we’re talking about our obscured eyes.

“Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad”. Oppression is what keeps you from realizing the hope you’re looking for. Oppression is the opposite of getting hope, the opposite of you realizing your quote-unquote dreams, your aspirations, your goals; all of that is chopped off, and that’s due to oppression. So when the oppression comes down on you and you cannot realize your dreams, it makes you mad, which is crazy.

But it says it maketh a wise man mad. The wise man knows that he’s not supposed to get caught up in this mess. As oppressed people, if you’re wise, you know where you came from, you know your history, you know what people you come from and what God you belong to. So when oppression comes, it makes the wise man get some sense and learn how to organize. The anger we express, the mad we get, we learn to organize and do the things we are doing now: bring forth solutions to our people and wake them up, so that one day we can get out of oppression.

An example: one of these unfair police killings, our brothers killed in the street, and everybody in the community upset and crying. But they let Peyton do all kinds of rampage, they let Dylann Roof do all kinds of rampage, and the worst thing is the news media tried to protect them, calling him a lone wolf, a lone gunman, a teenager, to make him seem like he’s not a grown man. They call Michael Brown a black man, but they call this murderous bastard a teenager. They want to turn Michael Brown into King Kong and make Peyton a sweet little angel that just got misguided. And those white men said no, we’re not crazy, we’re not deprived, we’re not a freak of nature, and the news was like, wait a minute, we’re trying to protect you, why don’t you accept that label? That’s the real ugliness we experience in this society.

It’s about time for us to face reality. We can’t be scared, brothers and sisters; the scriptures say the fearful will not make it into the kingdom. So it’s time to see reality for what it is and let go of the social construct BS.

If our people were really serious about being upset: our brother murdered over basically one cigarette, basically nothing. Our brothers are being made extinct; that’s generations of men, generations of people they’re killing off. You can’t tell me that this is not systematic. They know exactly what they’re doing: that’s genocide of your sons. And they say, oh, he had a gun. People that are licensed to carry guns, you know how much stuff you got to go through to get that? Ain’t nobody believing that, but they’ll put them to death anyway.

Black people are fearful and scared, and they fit what this Bible says. This is why the preachers need to tell the people (Gino Jennings, T.D. Jakes, Creflo, all of you): you need to be telling those Israelites in your church that they are the Israelites the Bible speaks of, and stop lying to them, because you’re going to pay for that. I don’t care how big your church is, if you don’t start dealing with God’s heritage properly and wake them up according to this Bible.

“And among these nations shalt thou find no ease”: among these nations the Israelites shall find no ease. “Neither shall the sole of thy foot have rest”: neither shall our people have rest. The people in the churches know they’re not first-class citizens at all: second class, third class, hell no class.

“But the Lord shall give thee there a trembling heart”: every nation we went into, especially this country here, we have a trembling heart and are scared to death. When that man was reading the KKK letter, I could see the fear in their eyes. They didn’t feel like the blood of Jesus would have stopped that man from coming in; he could have come in and done just like Dylann Roof and blown those people away. That’s the reason Dylann did it: so that you would feel like you have no protection. That’s terrorism. These people are experts in murder, yet we’re a hate group. The white man is an expert murderer, an expert terrorist. How in the hell are you going to take somebody’s land, and the people you stole it from, you don’t even hear them saying anything? That’s major terrorism.

“And failing of eyes”: there’s your vision gone again. Eyes represent vision: being able to plan, to organize, to assemble and do something for your people. When your eyes fail, you cannot muster any semblance of your intelligence to actually realize the hope you say you want.

“And sorrow of mind”: that’s the sick mind we read earlier, a sick mind because your hope is deferred, nonexistent.

“And thy life shall hang in doubt before thee”: that’s exactly how the people felt in that church, and the blood of Jesus didn’t mean a damn thing.

Here’s why this scripture was brought out. A lot of these people in the churches have heard it; they were there when we were standing outside bringing the word, so they know there are prophets trying to reach them. A lot of them know this already, but because of fear of persecution, fear of retribution, fear of marginalization and assassinations, they hold back. That’s how they get you to conform to lies and reject truth, regardless of what’s actually true; they’ll get you to believe lies and hate the truth, and if you’re standing on the side of truth, they hate you. That’s what Christ said: it is not you that they hate, they hate me because I am in you; don’t marvel that the world hates you, because it hated me. That’s a social construct that wants to get rid of Christ and wants to get rid of the Bible.

Our brothers and sisters in these churches have heard this truth; they know they’re the Israelites. So why won’t they do what this Bible says? Because they’re afraid of the repercussions. And if they’re afraid of that, they’ll have a cognitive dissonance: a disdain for something they are aware of, and they want to put it off. It’s like smoking cigarettes. Cigarettes are bad for you, they have it written that the surgeon general has determined that it causes cancer, and you have to ignore that to justify your continual smoking. You have to ignore the reality in order to keep following the same trends that lead you nowhere.

If our people knew they were the Israelites, what would they actually do? The next time another brother or sister gets killed, Sandra Bland or George Floyd, they would say: why don’t we keep the commandments of God as a people? Come Christmas, we ain’t buying a damn thing, and you get some respect. Come Easter, let the bunnies go, leave them rabbits alone; we don’t want no eggs; what does an egg have to do with a rabbit anyway? Come Thanksgiving, let the turkeys go. Cut all that off. But we are afraid to do that, because there’s a system out here called reward and punishment. They punish you when you go against the social construct, and they reward you if you’re in sin. A man says he wants to be a woman, and they reward him by passing laws; if you speak against that, you get punished, ostracized, marginalized, persecuted. That’s how we live. How in the hell is that first-class citizenship? This is reality, brothers and sisters; get hip to it.

“And thou shalt fear day and night”: the Israelites shall fear day and night. Who’s that at the door? That’s exactly the look they had on their faces. Every time you hear the white man call you, chills go through your spine, some of us, because if it comes from him it has meaning. Why? Because you were terrorized into associating him with authority.

“And shalt have none assurance of thy life”: the people in the church say they are absolved of what we’re reading, we’re in the blood of Jesus, we’re saved. That white man said you ought to have your tongue cut out, and the people in the church felt that. So don’t tell me about the white blood of Jesus. You’re terrorized people, just like the Bible says. Get hip to what the Bible is saying and come out of that foolishness.

They know it’s the truth. They know the history; they’ve seen the history of it being true. That’s why Dylann Roof did it: he didn’t kill everybody in the church. There were people in there that saw it go down. Could you imagine being in there rejoicing in the blood of Jesus, and bang bang bang bang? The people sitting in there that heard that are messed up for life, terrorized, and the word got out to every black church. Then all of a sudden a preacher reads a KKK letter, and you’re going to tell me the people ain’t going to feel that? They felt it. First-class citizens: come off that dope, come off that methadone that normalizes you to an ass whooping. That’s basically what they do: numb your senses to the reality that’s supposed to wake you up.

We’re dealing with the title: following God’s vision that’s beyond obscured eyes. The vision that’s in our eyes is deceptive because we were given the wrong lenses. We’re looking at a racist society that hates us. The scriptures say you shall be hated of all nations for my name’s sake. What in the world is wrong with people’s reading that they can’t understand what that means? It means what it says.

“That we should be saved from our enemies”: who’s the we? In case somebody says we don’t know who the we is. “And from the hand of all that hate us”: who hates us? The hate group called America, the hate group called the United States of America, the hate group called white folks, the hate group called the Arabs, the Chinese, the Japanese, all of those. The scriptures say we will be hated of all nations; all nations hate us.

“And from the hand of all that hate us”: the hand is the control of all that hate us. It is the same hand that sold us into captivity, that took us and sold us. That’s the reason this Bible is so beautiful. You’re not going to give me no doggone dope to make me think this Bible ain’t for us; the hell with you and your mama.

precepts.why:
From the hand of all that hate us, listen to what the scriptures say. “And he that stealeth a man”: were we stolen, brothers and sisters? Yes. “And selleth him”: were you sold?

And this damn bastard is going to say Deuteronomy 28 ain’t talking about us, that we sold ourselves. This doggone demon had to go all over, under a rock, to try to find something to refute the scriptures, and any of y’all that believe that got your head up a cow’s butt. How are you going to be sold when there’s no seller? How is it you’re going to be sold but there’s no buyer? The Bible says sold, with the -ed on the end, past tense: ‘ye shall be sold’. If you were sold, there was a seller and a buyer that bought you, paid for you like a piece of property. Don’t tell me that ain’t talking about us; you can stick your head in your own behind before I believe that mess.

“Or if he be found in his hand”: are we found in the white man’s hands, in our enemies’ hands? Yes. “He shall surely be put to death”: negroes don’t want that. We’re found in his hand; he put his name on us, for crying out loud. He said you’re my property, damn it. So we’re in his hands, and his hands are getting ready to get cut off by God. That is the hand of all that hate us in Luke 1:71, and the Negro don’t want this.

sense.text:
“The Lord shall smite thee with madness”: the Lord shall smite our people with madness, craziness, psychiatric problems, dope dealing, dope taking, and Christianity, that’s another one. Madness is Christianity: you’re just sitting up there with the Bible and all of a sudden you got the Holy Ghost, you got epilepsy.

“And blindness, and astonishment of heart”: this is the obscured eyes we’re talking about. We cannot perceive reality properly; we’re living in an illusion, a delusion.

Delusion is having false or unrealistic beliefs. An unrealistic belief is a white Jesus coming to save black people, when white whipped and raped and hung your behind; all of a sudden the white man is going to come from the midst of all that murder and blood and save you. Many black people are really white men in black face. When a negro comes up defending white supremacy Christianity, that’s not a black man, that’s a white man in a black body, because his mind is totally wiped out. As a man thinketh, that’s what he is, forget what he looks like on the outside: his mind is white supremacy, his mind is Christianity, his mind is doped up. You’re catching hell from A to Z: parents, children, your community all messed up, your daughters are hoes, your sons are drug dealers, and you don’t want some kind of resurrection from that. The white man said you’re all right, you don’t need to resurrect, because if you resurrect I don’t get paid; I need you to stay that way, in the blood of white Jesus.

This is what’s wrong with black people in the church, with the people in so-called Christianity. Christianity is white supremacy. The black people in the Christian church that are watching know this is the truth, but the cognitive dissonance is there: I can’t accept what I know is reality, because the minute I do, discomfort comes to me; I’m going to be ostracized, marginalized, persecuted. Christianity is false; it’s unrealistic. How in the world do you expect these people to deal with you with respect and honor when they brought you over here as property? They don’t see us like they see themselves; they’re always going to see you beneath them, and then you’re talking about being on an equal footing? You crazy as hell.

Even the constitution tells you: read the Dred Scott decision. They believe that thing is still in effect. They say the constitution cannot change its construction and meaning, that it must be carried on from the days it was formed and adopted, so the change of public opinion ain’t changing nothing. Even though they tell us we have certain rights, the 13th, 14th and 15th amendments, in reality that’s the reason your sons are dying for nothing and mass murderers are getting a trip to Burger King.

Delusional is maintaining fixed false beliefs even when confronted with facts. That’s what’s going on with the Christian right now. We read out of the Bible about black Jesus; that’s facts. But they’ll keep going with a social construct of lies, a lying concept, rather than deal with what we just read. It’s a psychiatric definition, meaning it deals with the mind. Christianity maintains lies even when confronted with facts; you can’t find a more accurate description of the Christian in the church. It’s damn near biblical. Tell the church people, family members, look, the Bible says Jesus is black, and they say don’t show me that, get that away from me.

And it says usually as a result of mental illness. That’s Deuteronomy 28:28: you’re sick; the people in the church are sick.

Read it again: madness, craziness, and astonishment of heart, astonishment of your mind. That reflects back to what we read earlier: hope deferred maketh the mind sick, because you ain’t going to get no hope in there, and the people know that. The psychiatric definition of delusion is exactly on point: they maintain false white supremacy called Christianity, and they know damn well they’re less than dogs in there. Even when confronted with the real facts of the Bible that say you don’t belong in this crack house, they still justify that mess.

Usually as a result of mental illness: that’s what’s wrong with our people. That inferiority complex taught to us in slavery is a mental illness, a damn near permanent sickness, and it’s going to take the real medicine of the Bible to get us out of that. The preacher has an obligation, especially a black preacher. He’s sick himself; he needs to be getting his medicine so he can help his people out. But he’s scared, because if he does that, he knows this wicked government is going to come against him. He knows that fear day and night, that trembling heart: a man reading the KKK letters and the people in his church scared.

The preacher has an obligation, especially a black preacher. He is sick himself; he needs to be getting his medicine so he can help his people out. But he is scared, because he knows that if he does it this wicked government is going to come against him. Fear day and night, a trembling heart: reading the KKK letters, and the people in this church are scared.

The blindness is in our eyes too. Following God’s vision that is beyond obscured eyes means seeing past what we have been trained not to see. The eyes don’t lie; the Bible has not been tampered with, your head has. The eyes see reality, but by the time the information goes through the brain, the brain says no, you didn’t see that, and you come out your mouth with something crazy. Put your arm up against your shoes: you are not black, you are brown. Hold a piece of paper up against the so-called white man: he is not white, he is red, red like that fire extinguisher. Because of a social construct everybody agreed that these people are white when they’re not white and that we are black when we’re not black. Ignoring facts when you are confronted with facts is mental illness: your eyes see what they see, but you won’t accept the reality.

Black is a common term we say, but white means purity, and these people ain’t pure nothing but Satan. They want to put us in a meat grinder and eat steak over our dead body. As a man thinketh so is he: our eyes have been distorted through the lens of obscurity, so we need corrective lenses, lenses set up to correct distorted vision, and the corrective lens is the Bible.

God created this earth for righteousness’ sake. He chose a righteous man, Adam, to establish his earth in righteousness, and Eve was to be his helper, his stay and his comfort, establishing righteousness by following the commandments God taught Adam and that Adam was to teach his wife; but she did not want to do that. God also put two boys in the Bible for a reason, Adam had Cain and Abel, to show the difference between righteousness and wickedness. It is time to clear up the vision and see what God is really showing us. What are we doing here in America? Our land is in Jerusalem. That means something happened, and we made somebody mad to cause it. That is what the people in the churches need to understand about why we are catching all this hell, brutality and murder.

We had to learn the negative before we can set up the positive, because you need contrast: good is set against evil. You cannot determine what is good if good is not set in contrast to evil. You don’t know what cold water is without getting burned by hot water, and you cannot tell what daylight is if you have never experienced night. That is why God put those two boys on this earth, and that is why his continuation has a period on it: once the fulfillment of his evil has reached its pinnacle, God has no more use for them. Round them all up, as in the book of Obadiah, burn them up and get rid of them. That is his fate, not ours, and you can’t do nothing to change it. The sick negro trying to pull him out the fire might burn up with him.

Contrast is the state of being strikingly different from something else, juxtaposed, the other end of it. Black people and white people are contrast to each other, and God set it up that way.

“As the clay is in the potter’s hand, to fashion it at his pleasure: so man is in the hand of him that made him”: man is in the hand of God that made him. That is contrast, good versus evil. The man he is fashioning is in the hand of the maker to do his purpose, “to render to them as liketh him best”: as he likes best, you are going to fulfill my will. He made the so-called white man to be the devil; he made him that way. He made you black men and women, Hispanic men and women, Native American Indian men and women, the jewels of God.

This is about Esau and Jacob. “That the purpose of God according to election might stand”: according to how God chose to fashion them. “Not of works”, not of what they did; God made this decision before they were even born, “but of him that calleth”, of the maker that called them to do what he made them to do.

“The elder shall serve the younger”: it was said unto Rebecca, and God made that decision before the children were even born. Now you see why they’ve got to get rid of this Bible. This is in the New Testament; why didn’t he read this in the church?
“Jacob have I loved”: Jacob is not everybody, Jacob is you. “But Esau have I hated”, and who is saying this? God. What in the world is a Klan walking around talking about someday being next to Jesus.
Is God unrighteous because, as the potter, he decided I want this part for my glory and I want the other one to move my bowels in? “God forbid.”

Now he gives the history, that he did it before with the Egyptians. “I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy”: don’t talk to me, shut up, I will do what I want to do because I am the man making the parts, I am the potter. I will have mercy on whom I choose to have mercy on, and compassion on whom I decide. The Bible says the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, so with that understanding there is no need to talk to me about nothing.

“So then it is not of him that willeth”: you cannot will to be the people of the Most High if you are not the Israelites; that is crystal clear. “Nor of him that runneth”: you can’t run a race to be God’s people. You can’t call yourselves Christians and talk about coming into the kingdom of the Lord; you are going as a slave, and they won’t last long. They get about a thousand years of slavery, then the Most High’s command is to wipe them all out, extinguish them.

“But of God that sheweth mercy”, and he shows mercy to Israel. With this understanding the obscurity on our mind, the self-hatred and the self-doubt, should begin to clear up, because the Bible tells you that you are the children of Jacob.

“Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up”: the same purpose, just like the way he did Pharaoh, is the way he is doing Esau. Before he destroyed Pharaoh he hardened his heart and he built him up; Pharaoh was feared as a god. When the midwives were charged to kill the male babies, they lied to Pharaoh, all praise to the Lord, and said these Hebrew women deliver before we can even get there. Pharaoh wanted them dead just like these people want us dead. They were looking to kill Moses, the deliverer, because they did not want the people taken out of bondage. The same thing happened in the time of Christ, and the same thing is happening right now.

I raised you up, Pharaoh, and I am going to do the same thing with Esau: give him the weapons, the technology, the guns, the power, so that everybody fears him like a god. That is why the people in the church are shook and scared. They don’t realize this man has a time limit like Pharaoh had a time limit.

“That I might shew my power in thee”: that is what he did when he destroyed Pharaoh’s army, and everybody knew the Most High had the power. The obscurity of the Israelites’ minds and eyes was cleared up after that, then they got stupid again in the wilderness. He brought everybody out of Egypt, rebellious negroes and all kinds of wickedness, but the Lord ain’t gonna take everybody on this trip. A lot of people ain’t coming out of this captivity. The only ones getting out of here are those that repented and keep these commandments; the rest of the people are going to die right here with their enemies.

“And that my name might be declared throughout all the earth”: that is why he is raising up Esau, so he can destroy Esau the same way. God caused this man to build the weapons to his own destruction. I don’t want to build a bomb; you’re going to build it anyway. I don’t want to press the button; you’re going to press the button.

“Therefore hath he mercy on whom he will have mercy”: God has mercy on whom he chooses, “and whom he will he hardeneth”, he hardens whom he chooses, like he did Pharaoh. That is the same way he is dealing with this arrogant beast today. God made him that way; he is the cherub the Bible speaks of, the anointed cherub, the evil one.

This is the argument: “Why doth he yet find fault?” How in the world are you going to find fault with the white man if you made him to be evil? How could you find fault with Pharaoh if you hardened Pharaoh’s heart against you? Understand the kind of power you serve: the Most High makes these people resist him so that he can smash them in your presence. He builds this man up, gives him the weapons and the technology so he gets big, bad and nasty, and then the Lord kills him right before your eyes. You say what kind of fairness is that, because you don’t understand that God creates the nations for his purpose. He didn’t create you for that, but he created him for that.

That is why he said don’t be trying to marry them, because you don’t know what you’re marrying. The Bible says if you get up with these other nations they will turn your mind away from the Lord. In Deuteronomy he was talking about the different African groups, but it goes with all of them, because none of them are the Israelites. You are the Israelites: marry your own, be with your own people.

“For who hath resisted his will?” If God made him to be evil and wicked, how in the world can he deviate from the plan and the program God put into his spirit? God made the man a man; you are going to tell them I’m a woman, and that ain’t gonna last long. No matter how much a dog tries to be a cat, it is still a dog.

“Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against God?” In other words, shut the hell up: who are you to open your mouth against what I do? “Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus?” God made the pot to move his bowels in; can the pot jump up and say why did you make me the toilet? The pot can’t say nothing, because God the maker made it that way.

“Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump”: everybody came out of Adam. “To make one vessel unto honour”: to make one people that I want to honour, and another to move my bowels in. One vessel to drink my wine out of, and the other vessel to move my bowels in.

Now he explains why he is doing what he is doing. “What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known”: God wants to make his power known. “Endured with much longsuffering”: the Most High has emotions. People are so sick they say God can’t hate and God can’t suffer, as if we could have emotions and God could not, which would make us superior to him. What did he endure? “The vessels of wrath fitted to destruction”, and that is Esau. Even their own Bible dictionary, which they wrote, admits that of all Israel’s neighbours Edom was given no promise of mercy from God.

God is enduring with much longsuffering because he is trying to wake you Israelites up.

precepts.why:
“The Lord is not slack concerning his promise”, his promise to deliver Israel. “As some men count slackness”: some men say the Lord is not going to do what he said he would do.

“But is longsuffering”: that longsuffering is the endurance the Lord is dealing with. Longsuffering to whom? “To us-ward”: to the Israelites, black men and black women, Hispanic men and Hispanic women, North American Indian men and women, the twelve tribes of Israel. He is longsuffering for you to wake up.

“Not willing that any should perish”: not willing that any of his beloved shall perish. The Lord loves you, brothers; the Lord loves you, sisters; the hell with the white man. “But that all should come to repentance”: God wants you to come to repentance, and that is the reason he sent us into this punishment. He put this punishment on us to wake us up, that we come to repentance; otherwise we would never have been here, we would never have left home.

This is longsuffering again. “The Lord shall go forth as a mighty man, he shall stir up jealousy like a man of war”: this is God talking. “He shall prevail against his enemies”, and God’s enemies are your enemies, because we are one in Christ, one in the real Jesus, one with the Most High.

“I have long time holden my peace”: that is longsuffering right there. Do you know what it is to hold your peace a long time, when you want to say something and get loose? But God cannot break his word. God gave a time limit, a dispensation of time; he has boundaries he appoints in his prophecies, and he does not bend them or break them. That doesn’t mean the Lord enjoys seeing you down here messed up like this; God don’t like that. “I have been still, and refrained myself”: he is holding himself back, because he wants to break the prophecies to get in and kill.

“Now will I cry”: that now means he is free to kick ass. I am free from my prophecies, not bound by my word anymore, because it is finished. “Like a travailing woman”: that is how angry the Lord is going to be. It is the one coming from Edom in Isaiah 63 with his garments dyed, who trod the winepress alone, with the blood splattered all over his garments. “I will destroy and devour at once”: when he is free to do this he is going to get loose on our enemies.

This is what we want; who in the world doesn’t want this? The sick negro says if the white man can’t be saved I don’t want salvation; then you are just going to die with them. We already understand that two-thirds of our people get liquidated anyway, as long as that salvation keeps on coming.

sense.text:
Back to that longsuffering: “What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction”.

Fitted to destruction is the tailor-made suit of destruction, and it is fitted for Esau. Nobody else could put that garment on but him.

Look at that word, the vessels of wrath. A vessel is something you channel something through. God is going to channel his anger through Esau, he is going to channel his destructive power through Esau, like he did through Pharaoh. That’s the reason: ‘for the same purpose have I raised you up’, so that I can show my power by destroying you, and that my name might be declared all over the earth.

You mean to tell me the white man ain’t ruling no more? Where is he? He gone, damn, he’s gone. We can have some peace now.

The trees are going to say that; this one scripture comes before getting back to Sirach 33.

“The Lord hath broken the staff of the wicked”, because his time is up. The Lord has broken the staff, the power, of the white man; that’s what this chapter is going into. This is so beautiful because nobody can refute it. They say, y’all making the Bible say what you want it to say. No: when you get to verse 14 on down it’s crystal clear that it’s only talking about him. It ain’t even talking about the other nations. 100 percent Esau, 100 percent him.

The wicked is the white man: ‘the earth is given unto the hand of the wicked, and then shall that wicked be revealed’, who opposed God. “And the sceptre of the rulers”: the sceptre of the ruler is the power seat. All of that glory, he’s going to get rid of all of that. He ain’t going to rule nothing.

“He who smote the people in wrath”: who smote the nations in anger? Talk to me, Esau. You go in another man’s land and tell him where he can and cannot fly his own planes, a no-fly zone. Who the hell put that up there? You just go on top of people that you don’t like. You rule the nations in anger, then you set up your foreign policy to make sure they never get any kind of protection to protect themselves.

“With a continual stroke”: the continual killing, a continual stroke of oppression. That’s called foreign policy.

“He that ruled the nations in anger”: it’s personal. And see how social constructed our people’s minds are, where common sense don’t even work. The United Nations building is a world court, a body where nations sit down and make decisions and bring up cases about what country did wrong to that country: this country did this, that country did that, we put an embargo against them, we put sanctions against them. So the building where justice is supposed to be happening is sitting on stolen property. Where is the Native American Indian man in the court? ‘Hey, you bastards are on my land, get the hell off.’ They’re in the bathroom of their own house, relegated, but yet you want to set up a court talking about what this country did wrong to that one, in a damn territory that the building is sitting on that is stolen. And they ask, what school did you go to? Certainly you didn’t get this kind of thinking going through our schools.

“Is persecuted, and none hindereth”: that’s what’s going to happen. The Most High got that part set up too. He’s going to start sending these terrorists over here, which ain’t got nothing to do with the negro. The scriptures say all these nations shall take up a parable against him and say, ‘woe be unto him that increases that which is not his’, and the scriptures use the term caterpillars. These people are going to come in here, white boys that look like Arabs, with the Arab philosophy in them. They’re going to set up cells, sleeper cells and all of that. That’s why they’re trying to fix some borders up. They ain’t worried about the Mexican.

This is the point: the trees are going to be glad. “The whole earth is at rest”: when this devil goes down the whole earth is going to be at rest. Think of a bird. A bird has wings to fly; put him in a cage and he’s a damn bird mad as hell. He got wings and all he can do is jump from this perch to that perch while your big stupid self is looking at him.

“And is quiet: they break forth into singing”: the earth breaks forth into singing, rejoicing.

“Yea, the fir trees rejoice at thee”: the fir tree is going to rejoice when this man goes down. It’s going to literally say it, the fir trees “and the cedars of Lebanon, saying, Since thou art laid down”, since thou art destroyed, Esau, ‘no fellow is come up against us’, because nobody else is the devil but you. That’s what the trees are saying. So the trees got spirit too.

So now they call that hate teaching. If I’m the shepherd of the sheep, and the sheep are with me, and the wolf is over there saying, come on into my church and learn the doctrine of the wolf, you’ll be lying in green pastures, all right. But then they hear me say, hey sheep, come over here, stay away from that wolf. The wolf will say, you’re a hate teacher, because we fixed it so that you can’t get bit anymore.

Back to Sirach 33: “As the clay is in the potter’s hand, to fashion it at his pleasure: so man is in the hand of him that made him, to render to them as liketh him best.” He renders to these pots that he made as he decided for them to do.

“Good is set against evil”: this is the point made in the beginning. We would not be able to tell what good is if we did not have to go through the evil. So this wicked man has a purpose. His job was to show us what it is like being on this earth when God’s laws are not enforced, and you see what it has done: it has destroyed everything, including the minds of the people here. You got a man born with testicles and he says he wants to be a woman, and they say that’s okay. Here’s a woman born with breasts, vagina and every damn thing else, and she told my son she wants to be a man. That’s not God’s laws, and that kind of sick thinking will destroy everything.

“And life against death”: you cannot appreciate life unless you know what death is.

“So is the godly against the sinner”: how could we determine what godliness is without the understanding of sin? That’s the reason why we had to go through all this evil, to learn. “And the sinner against the godly”: so the Lord set up these trials.

The understanding behind all of this is to illuminate the benefits of good against the detriment of evil, like the advantages of the day, where you can see clearly, against the perils of the night, where you’re most likely to get mugged and robbed. You learn to appreciate the daytime when you’ve experienced what happens at night. That’s what we are experiencing, living on this earth with this vile beast.

They really want to condemn this because of adjectives that are hurtful, but it’s only what these people do. Nothing violent is being said, just facts. They want to gather a consensus to shut truth down, to have people believe in a social construct and a concept that is against reality, and to cause us to deny facts like what we’re reading.

That is why the Bible records that in the kingdom there will be no night there, meaning no alternative to good: no evil. That is not speaking of physical day against night, but spiritually of good and evil.

This is about clearing up the confusion in our eyesight, about not understanding the program of God. The truth that shall make you free is knowing the plan of God, knowing the vision of God, following the vision of God that is beyond your obscured thinking, beyond your obscured vision, because you’re not seeing the Bible properly. Our people shall be all righteous: that’s where this is going.

“Violence shall no more be heard in thy land”: violence shall no more be heard in our land when this is all over. “Wasting nor destruction within thy borders”: no wasting and destruction within the borders of the kingdom of Israel. “But thou shalt call thy walls Salvation”: we shall call our walls Salvation, and our gates Praise.

“The sun shall be no more thy light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee: but the Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light”. This is talking about the commandments of God: the everlasting light means the commandments are going to be forever. “And thy God thy glory”: the power is going to be our glory; the glory is going to be upon Israel.

“Thy sun shall no more go down”: thy sun, thy son, your son, your wisdom, shall no more go down, “neither shall thy moon withdraw itself: for the Lord shall be thine everlasting light”. This is the Bible’s commandments.

“And the days of thy mourning shall be ended”: the days of our sorrow shall be ended. This is what Isaiah 14 was talking about.

Since we’re talking about sorrow and the days of mourning being ended, this is Isaiah 14.

“For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel”: he will still choose Israel even though we broke his laws. The Most High says, I prefer that all of you come to repentance. That’s the mercy; he didn’t give that to nobody else, that’s only Israel. “And set them in their own land”: the Lord is going to set us back in our glory.

“And the strangers shall be joined with them”: the nations shall be joined with us. That’s all the other nations; they’re going to learn to keep these commandments. “And they shall cleave to the house of Jacob”: they’re going to cleave to this Bible, because they’re going to be taught this Bible, taught how to keep these commandments.

“And the people shall take them, and bring them to their place”: the Israelites shall take them, and we’re going to bring them to our place. “And the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids”: slaves, like they had us. We’re going to possess the nations as slaves. They’re going to be made to build up our walls, and the nation and the kingdom that refuse to build our walls, the scriptures say, shall be utterly wasted.

“And they shall take them captives, whose captives they were”: we shall take them captives who had us as captives. We was all the nations’ captives.

“And they shall rule over their oppressors”: this right here is therapy. All that craziness read at the start of the class, this is the redemptive therapy. This is the restitution I need, the reparations, the repairing I need. ‘We give you 40 acres and a mule.’ No, man, I don’t want that; I want the justice of the Most High. Keep your money, honey. Whatever money you got, you stole it, so how are you giving me back my own money? No, I need your behind in slavery. See, God believes in real justice, and that’s what you got to want.

“And it shall come to pass in the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow”: this is the days of mourning read in Isaiah 60:20: thy sun shall no more go down, neither shall thy moon withdraw herself, for the Lord shall be thine everlasting light, and the days of thy mourning shall be ended. That is what we’re reading here.

The Lord shall give us rest from our sorrow. That’s what we read in Deuteronomy earlier: among these nations shalt thou find no ease, neither shall the sole of your foot have rest. In all of the nations that we serve captivity in we got no rest; they worked us to death. Now the Lord is saying he will give us rest from our sorrow, from our broken minds, rest from this false hope that we were trying to get, that was constantly deferred, all that crying and begging. The Lord said, I’m going to take you away from all that. You ain’t got to beg these people for nothing; I’m getting ready to give you the whole planet earth, and them as well.

“And from thy fear”: the KKK is knocking, he’s around the church, he’s going to come and get us. He’s going to take us away from that fearful spirit.

“And from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve”: here’s a good example of a social construct trying to obscure your eyes from reality. Hard bondage, not just regular bondage. What people on the planet can you attribute that verse to? Nobody but us. God put it in the Bible like that because he wants you to know, I’m talking to you. Your names were taken from you, your heritage was taken from you, your children were taken from you, your lives were taken, your land was taken, your riches, your diamonds, everything was taken from you, then you were made a slave, and they ain’t treated us right since. So how the hell are you going to put that on somebody else? The Lord said he’s going to take us from that hard bondage, wherein we were made to serve, right here in Babylon the great.

“That thou shalt take up this proverb against the king of Babylon”: the proverb is this whole scripture. We are to take this whole scripture and bring it against the king of Babylon, the so-called white man in America. That’s the reason why we’re in the church: we need to wake our people up, because the Lord is going to destroy this whole system.

“And say, How hath the oppressor ceased!”: how is it that you’re losing your kingdom? God is mocking him.

“The golden city ceased!” Why is America called the golden city? ‘I want to go to America because the streets are paved with gold.’ America became the golden city because she robbed everybody else’s riches, stole them and brought all her riches here, then brought us: the souls of men, and slaves also. Babylon the great has that; that’s what Revelation was talking about. And what else made it golden? The talents we were stripped of. The most valuable resource is black people. They took our music from us, took our dress code from us, took all our fine theater and arts and inventions, everything we’ve done, and left us on the ground, and still call us like we ain’t nothing, when we are literally the jewels of God. Don’t you women ever forget that. Don’t you men ever forget that.
“The Lord hath broken the staff of the wicked, and the sceptre of the rulers”: we went through this earlier. It proves that this chapter is against him.

precepts.why:
We was all the nations’ captives; the book of Luke tells you that. And the white man is going to be dead, don’t worry about him: he’s going to do his captivity and he’s going to get exterminated.

“And they shall fall by the edge of the sword”: the Israelites shall fall by the edge of the sword when we disobey God. This was the judgment that came as a result of breaking the laws and the commandments that Moses told us to keep.

“And shall be led away captive into all nations”: how many nations? All nations. We shall be led into captivity into all nations. That’s the New Testament; how come they ain’t reading this?

“And Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles”: Jerusalem shall be walked upon by so-called Jews, “until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled”: until their bounds is done, until their time is finished, until their time limit is over. ‘Thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass’; that’s why it’s said that way. When their time is fulfilled they’re going to Psalms 149, they’re going to Isaiah 14. That’s where they’re going, that’s what we’re reading: “they shall take them captives, whose captives they were”.

“How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning!”: how art thou falling out of your kingdom, how has the oppressor ceased. “How art thou cut down to the ground”: that’s what Revelation was talking about, he was cast out. “Which didst weaken the nations!” What did this bastard do? He weakened all the nations, dropping bombs on them. And who’s saying this? The Most High.

sense.text: Back to Isaiah 60 now that we have that understanding about the days of our mourning being ended: “Thy sun shall no more go down; neither shall thy moon withdraw itself: for the Lord shall be thine everlasting light, and the days of thy mourning shall be ended.” The days of our mourning shall be ended, and the Lord says that our sun shall no more go down and our moon shall not withdraw herself.

precepts.why:
“And there appeared a great wonder in heaven; a woman”: this woman is Israel. This is us in our kingdom; this is history here. “A woman clothed with the sun”: we’re going to find out what the sun is. “And the moon under her feet”: that’s the sun and the moon again, that shall never go out. “And upon her head a crown of twelve stars”, meaning the twelve tribes of Israel.

Read again after Proverbs 6:23, that’s the point: the woman is clothed with the sun, so we will be clothed with the commandments of God. ‘Thy kingdom come, thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.’

What do this sun and this moon represent? “For the commandment is a lamp”: commandment doesn’t have an s on it. The commandment of God is a lamp, “and the law is light”: that’s the sun and the moon read in Isaiah 60 and Revelation 12. The law of God is light.

“And reproofs of instruction are the way of life”: these commandments of God, this Bible, are reproofs of instruction. That’s the way of life for us, to be reproved, to be corrected by God’s commandments.

For example, the pleasure of sin is met with the punishment of correction: this is contrasting reproof. Reproofs are understood by contrasts. We get to understand the benefits of being corrected when that judgment comes on us, and it teaches us not to break God’s laws.

sense.text:
“Thy sun shall no more go down; neither shall thy moon withdraw itself”: the sun and the moon of the woman in Revelation 12 are the commandment and the law, and they shall never go out. “For the Lord shall be thine everlasting light”: the Lord shall be our everlasting light.

“And the days of thy mourning shall be ended”: the days of our sadness and sorrow, of our broken minds and our deferred hope, shall be ended.

“Thy people also shall be all righteous”: our people shall be all righteous. “They shall inherit the land for ever”: this is the commandments the Lord is laying out for us, and he says that we shall inherit the land for ever.

“The branch of my planting”: the branch of God’s planting. You’re the vine that God set up. “The work of my hands, that I may be glorified”: he wants the whole planet earth to know how he’s going to beautify his people, that he may be glorified when he shows his mercy on his vessel Israel.

“The work of my hands” is the part to bring out. We, the righteous seed, were made by the authority of God to be in his image and likeness. That’s what he made us, us men.

precepts.why:
“What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction”: the Lord is going to destroy this so-called white man for your benefit, because he’s the vessels of God’s wrath.

Now find out what other vessel God has: “And that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy”. After he destroys Esau, God is going to make his glory known upon the vessels of mercy. The vessels of mercy is Jacob, the twelve tribes of Israel. He’s going to make known his glory on his vessel, the Israelites.

“Which he had afore prepared unto glory”: since he said let there be light, it was already ordained that you were going to be his people. So what are these people in these crack houses called church talking about? The Israelites were always to be glorified. That’s the reason why he named you Israel: you are the princes of God, princes and princesses of God, the children of the Most High.

That white man don’t want us to have that at all. He’s going to scrape up a bunch of red and say these are the Jews. No: you’re the Jews, you’re the Israelites, you’re the people of God. That is “the work of my hands, that I may be glorified”: when God shows his mercy on his vessel Israel.

“And God said, Let us make man in our image”: let us, the angels, the black God, the black Christ and the black angels. If man is going to be made in God’s image, and he’s going to make him out of the dirt that’s in the garden, what color is that dirt? Real brown, damn near black, that rich beautiful dark soil. That’s the beauty of black people. The emphasis on black has to be made because our minds have been warped to hate this, so it has to be overcompensated. And the Most High has beauty in all the tribes of Israel.

“After our likeness”: out of his express image. “And let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth”. Adam was made in the image of God, so you can understand the black man.

God formed us from his thoughts. The way he fashioned Adam, he pictured Adam in his mind: how to put his arms here, his head here, and fashioned him in the likeness of God. Your body has a purpose. The man was made directly from God, and the women come out of man. When he fashioned man, he fashioned him to be a reflection of what he would look like. That’s why Daniel 7 and 9 describes him with a head and a body that had a garment on, and a head of woolly hair, pure wool: that’s a man’s body in a celestial form, angelic, but still a body. When he made man, he made man in that same form.

Before he made man, he had to think about the functions of man: how his hands would be used, how his feet and legs are made and how the two operate so he can move from A to B. Look how he designed the eyes and the ears. He gave you two ears and the ability called a stereo effect: close your eyes and you can hear sounds to the left and to the right, and know where a sound came from because it reaches one ear before the other. God knew that when he made you; no white man created that. He put eyes in your head that take imagery and form it into information that feeds the brain and says, if I keep walking I’m going to fall into a ditch. There’s intelligence in that eyesight. And we have allowed the system to mess every damn thing up, to cause us to abuse our bodies.

You women: why did God fashion you the way he fashioned you? He didn’t put your vagina here; he put it way under there, where before a man gets to it he’s got to go through some stuff. If you talk some BS and allow him to get there, you have to contort your body to let him in. He put it there because it’s not supposed to be easy access, and you’ve got to have a head that understands you don’t just go mess over what God made. God gave the woman breasts with nipples to feed the babies that come out of her womb. That’s no play thing.

And the man: God gave you the intelligence to use your hands to fashion materials out of the ground. Everything you see outside of vegetation, water and dirt, you had to see in your mind first. A chair doesn’t exist until you create it in your mind and think what elements in this earth you can manipulate: pull up iron, pull up cotton, make clothes for our body, make a house. All of that had to come from a thought. Then God gave you a body with hands to take the vision in your head and materialize it, and now it’s reality: chairs, houses, clothing, buildings. That’s how God made you. And he built your body in a way that works with the female.

God gave you that intelligence. How the hell are you going to let this demonic beast turn your bodies into garbage? You’re not garbage. You’re going to allow some stupidness on social media to cause you to abuse your sister, and cause the sister with no damn sense to allow somebody to mess over her because she don’t know what God created? It’s a sick society. You better find out what this Bible is talking about, fast.

sense.text: “And now what hast thou to do in the way of Egypt, to drink the waters of Sihor? or what hast thou to do in the way of Assyria, to drink the waters of the river?” We’re taking on the philosophy of our enemies. Egypt was our enemy and Assyria was our enemy, and we’re listening to the other nations giving us counsel when God is your counselor.

“Thine own wickedness shall correct thee”: your own wickedness shall correct you, by following them and ignoring God. “And thy backslidings shall reprove thee”: your backsliding, your disobedience, shall reprove you, shall correct you.

“Know therefore and see that it is an evil thing and bitter, that thou hast forsaken the Lord thy God”: we have forsaken the Lord, forsaking this beautiful knowledge he gave us. “And that my fear is not in thee”: the fear of God is not in us.

“For of old time I have broken thy yoke, and burst thy bands”: that’s what the Lord did when he took us out of Egypt and out of the Assyrian captivity. He burst our yokes of iron and busted us out of captivity.

“And thou saidst, I will not transgress”: we promised we would not break the laws of God again. But we end up going right back into the same vomit, the same filth, and did it all over again, until the Lord got really mad and had to put us in more captivity: captivity after captivity, because we never learned.

“When upon every high hill and under every green tree thou wanderest, playing the harlot”: we played the harlot with the nations. You know what it means to play the harlot? Men and women, we open our behind and let Egypt bang us, we let America bang us, we let these nations bang us and rape us.

“Yet I had planted thee a noble vine”: God said, I planted you a noble people. I planted you with my hands to be noble. What the hell are you doing giving yourselves to nothing, when I made you my jewels? “Wholly a right seed”: I made you holy and a right seed.

“How then art thou turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine unto me?” I created you noble, I gave you my laws, I made you above everybody. How the hell do you turn into the degenerate plant of a strange vine that I don’t even recognize? That’s what the Lord said, and that’s how we act: like beasts. And we’re the jewels of God. Nowhere in the world are we supposed to be dealing with each other the way we deal, looking the way we look, acting the way we act.

He fashioned us to be like him, and he sent his Son to redeem us. What kind of love beats that? He said, you are my chosen, and you broke my laws, and I got mad and cast you away; but I love you so much I’m going to send my only begotten Son to be the lamb. Nothing else could be sacrificed to bring you back to me; the only one I can send is my own Son, who doesn’t have spot or blemish. You’re the world the Lord is trying to bring back, to give you a second chance. And the ones of our people that reject this salvation Christ is bringing, you deserve death.

precepts.why:
This is the more sore punishment, and it shows the love Christ had for us and the Most High had for us in sending his Son. The beauty he made you with, he fashioned with his hands to be his people. How dare you women allow somebody to mess over you? How dare you brothers not deal with your nation properly?

Under the old law of Moses, the laws of sacrifice, there were certain sins you could not bring an animal for. Those laws that said his blood shall be upon him meant your blood had to be spilled, because there was no remission of sins without blood. If the blood of an ox, a lamb or a goat could not redeem you, your blood was required, and when your blood spills, you’re dead. If two witnesses said you committed adultery, you died.

So it was with the woman the Pharisees brought, saying they caught her in the very act. The judgment for her was death. But where’s the man at? Who did she commit adultery with, some figure in space? The wicked Pharisees brought the woman and left the man alone; wicked as hell. Christ said he who is without sin cast the first stone, and nobody was without sin. He said, woman, where are thine accusers? None, Lord. Neither do I accuse you: go and sin no more. Keep the commandments. That showed the mercy that was beyond the law of Moses. Yet this filthy Christian BS allows the people to stay in sin, telling them God did away with the laws, and the people following that filthy preacher are going to get killed.

“He that despised Moses’ law died without mercy”: he that broke Moses’ law, the old covenant, died without mercy. The man and the woman that committed adultery, the law said they shall surely be put to death; No chance to say something, no mistrial. “Under two or three witnesses”: two or three witnesses said you did this and that, and it’s going down, boom. Imagine some of the sins we’ve committed falling under this. Brought up front during the time of Moses and convicted, how would you feel? Scared, trembling, scared to death.

“Of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing”: the blood of the new covenant. You counted the sacrifice of Christ as an unholy thing. Now you have a chance to repent from sins you could not have been redeemed from under the law of Moses; but if you break what Christ did, that’s worse than what happened in the time of Moses. Y’all telling me how terrible Moses is? This is a much sorer punishment.

“And hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace”: the spirit of grace is mercy. Grace is the time for you to get your ish together; you didn’t have that in the time of Moses. Now you’ve got time to repent, like it says in Peter: I want all my people to repent, because I’m longsuffering for you. That’s how much God loves you. That’s what Christ gave that woman: mercy. She was supposed to be dead, and he said, I’m going to give you mercy, but stop sinning. That’s in the New Testament, for you filthy Christians.

This was just one example of how far we strayed from God’s creation. We became strange to God: the degenerate plant of a strange vine.

sense.text:
All of these preachers and all of these churches have Bibles in them, and in the Bible there’s a real judgment about our people not receiving this word, and on the preacher. It’s out of love that we’re trying to reach our people, but our people are so fearful of the enemy that they will ignore scripture, because they’re still trying to be in accord with a social construct: the social engineering that causes our people to follow lies.

“Woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture!” Woe means destruction: destruction to the preachers. How do they scatter the sheep of God? By not telling them that they’re the Israelites, and having them jumping around, grown men twirling around like they’re on fire, like a James Brown concert, just throw the cape on them. He’s on fire with the Holy Ghost? No.

“Saith the Lord”: because you are the heritage of God. We were brought into captivity because we broke God’s laws. The preacher is supposed to be telling the people what’s going on with the condition of the people, like the Bible says: what is our iniquity that we did against God that caused all this evil to happen upon us? He’s supposed to tell them that you and I broke the laws of God and he cast us over here through slave ships and slavery and scattered us all around. Because he doesn’t want to tell them this, the people are going to die, because the wages of sin is death. But the charge for their dying is going to be on the preacher’s head. That’s why it starts off by saying destruction to the preacher: for scattering the Israelites into lies, into social constructs.

“Therefore thus saith the Lord God of Israel against the pastors that feed my people”: against the pastors, not for the pastors. “Ye have scattered my flock”: you have scattered my people into lies, into Christianity, into false hope. You did that, preacher, with your lying mouth. “And driven them away”: a shepherd is supposed to gather the people unto the Most High; he’s scattering them away into filth and foolishness, and the Bible is clearly talking about them.

“And have not visited them”: you have not visited them with the Bible. As it says in Luke, blessed be the Lord God of Israel, for he has visited and redeemed his people. You’re supposed to visit the people with their heritage, with the Bible, with who they are.

“Behold, I will visit upon you the evil of your doings, saith the Lord”: I will visit upon you filthy, wicked, lying preachers the evil of your doings. You get mad; I don’t give a damn. The Most High is going to get you right.

“And I will gather the remnant of my flock”: the Lord is not going to allow the preacher to destroy the elect. It’s like the blitzes we’re going on; this is of God. The people in those crack houses hear God calling them out, and they’re going to respond, and the Lord said, I’m going to gather you out of there: the remnant of his people that are going to repent, the one third that’s being slain by those false ideologies in the churches telling them they can eat pork and commit fornication. They’re not being taught God’s laws.

“Out of all countries whither I have driven them”: all the countries where we served captivity. In the same places where we were serving captivity, the Most High is going to set up sanctuaries for these people to come out of those witch covens and come to the Most High. “And will bring them again to their folds”: that’s what a shepherd is supposed to do, bring them to the fold of God and get them out of those lying prisons they call church.

precepts.why:
“Son of man, I have made thee a watchman”: a watchman is a preacher, a prophet, a man that’s responsible, a shepherd who watches over the sheep. You don’t scatter them, you gather them. “Unto the house of Israel: therefore hear the word at my mouth”: the Most High was talking through the prophets, through the watchmen.

“And give them warning from me”: this is what we’re telling TD Jakes and Creflo Dollar and a whole lot of them out there, and they’ve been trying to run. This message goes to them: we’re giving you pastors warning from God. You hear us reading the Bible, you see it plain, but you’re like that definition said: a social construct, believing in a concept that exists but not in objective reality. The reality we can all see is that we’re the Israelites, and you ignore it even when you’re presented with facts.

“When I say unto the wicked, Thou shalt surely die”: you’re breaking God’s laws, telling people they can eat pork and swine, talking craziness about the split hoof. You crazy as hell. “And thou givest him not warning”: that is why we’re doing what we’re doing, why we’re outside your church, trying to warn you. Bishop Nathanyel came in the spirit of peace: you’re my brothers, we’re trying to deal with the problems in our community. The church is a big place where people gather, and they’re being slain by those lies, so we’re trying to help you deal with them properly. You want to malign and marginalize us instead; you’re going to pay for that. Don’t look at our skin color and say we’re not as great as white folks.

“Nor speakest to warn the wicked from his wicked way, to save his life”: it’s a wicked thing to tell the people they don’t have to follow the commandments of God, and a wicked thing to not tell them they’re the Israelites, especially when you’re entrusted with the Bible. We’re not trying to take your congregation. We want to save your life through Christ, and we want you to give the people the medicine to save their lives. You’re our people; we ain’t got no hatred for you. We love our brothers and sisters in those churches, but they have to know who they are and that they are responsible for keeping the commandments of God. That’s what the law requires of the nation of Israel, and that never left.

“The same wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at thine hand”: if we don’t tell you, this is the judgment on us. The Most High said, if you’ve got this truth and you’re entrusted with this Bible, go out there and wake the people up. Most of them are tied up in these churches, and you preachers are the barrier, blocking them from what you yourself could give them if you would only come and work with your brothers. The hell with Esau, the hell with the white folks: this is about our people. Ride on the wave of lies and you’re going to get dealt with, not by us, we’re just mortal men for now, but the judgment is going to come from God.

“Yet if thou warn the wicked, and he turn not from his wickedness, nor from his wicked way”: this is where we’re at. We’re warning you, but you refuse to turn from your sin. You keep people in Christianity, keep teaching Christmas. Christmas, Halloween and Thanksgiving ain’t holidays in the Bible for the Israelites to keep; God says, I hate those feast days. God gave us feast days in the Bible, and that’s what you’re supposed to teach. But you’re afraid of marginalization, persecution and getting shut down, so you’re busy trying to please the enemy rather than do the work God commanded you to do as a leader, preacher and teacher.

“He shall die in his iniquity; but thou hast delivered thy soul”: you shall die in your iniquity, because we warned you. We’ve delivered our soul: we told you, we warned you, and if you don’t want to listen, it’s on you.
